newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - April 7.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Monday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Bankers Trust said it planned to buy stock brokerage Alex. Brown for stock valued at $1.7 billion.
* Microsoft agreed to acquire WebTV, which provides Internet information to television sets, for $425 million in stock and cash.
* America Online is in talks to buy CompuServe for up to $1.2 billion in stock.
* The Federal Communications Chairman and local carriers rejected a plan by AT&T, Bell Atlantic and NYNEX to change the fees local phone companies get for connecting long-distance telephone calls.
* More people are entering the U.S. workforce, one possible reason why the U.S. economy has grown while inflation has remained restrained.

* The U.S. Federal Trade Commission rejected an offer from Staples to get rid of 63 stores to meet antitrust criteria and tried to persuade the company not to salvage its proposed purchase of Office Depot.
* A United Auto Workers strike at a key General Motors plant in Oklahoma City, Okla. halted production of the Chevrolet Malibu.
* Boeing is examining how to double its 737 output and plans to boost its airliner production rate by 10 percent above already-announced levels.
* MESA Inc and Parker & Parsley agreed to merge in a stock deal forming one of the nation's largest independent oil and gas exploration and production companies.
* Union leaders at AMR Corp's American Airlines expect pilots to ratify a new contract by early May.
* Albert Dunlop, chairman of Sunbeam, has started exploring options including a possible sale of the company or an acquisition.

* A class action tobacco lawsuit settlement by Ligget, a unit of Brooke Group, is getting more interest because the Alabama judge who gave the deal preliminary approval is seen as being too willing to clear such agreements.
* Knight-Ridder plans to buy four newspapers from Walt Disney for $1.65 billion, an action seen as a change in its strategy to diversity.
* Heard on the Street: Some investors thought the oil giants would offer a safe harbor from market turbulence. Instead, they've offered more turbulence.

* Credit markets: How low can bond prices go? Bond prices tumbled Friday on the release of strong economic data -- pushing up the 30-year bond's interest rate to 7.12 percent -- and many bond investors and analysts are beginning to fret that rising rates and steady losses could be around for at least the next several months.
